messages:
irene: Heads up — after the v2.14.3 runtime rollout this morning I'm seeing a sustained p99 jump on text-generation for a subset of tenants. Noted around 09:20 UTC in canary cohort C2.
sam: Seeing same in grafana. p95 is okay but p99 ~2.8s -> ~6.1s on long sequences. Links: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ABCD/runtime-latency and jaeger: https://jaeger.redwood.example/trace/xyz
nina: Are these cold-kvcache requests or hot-path?
irene: Mostly hot-path, KV hit ratio didn't change much, but there are more blocked waits on dma-io in the flamegraphs.
charlie: Any recent kernel selector / scheduling changes in this rollout? we touched the async-kv prefetch logic in the runtime binary.
sam: Yes, v2.14.3 included async prefetch + a new stressproxy affinity change (PR #4129). Could be interaction with our NIC driver.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Successful canary rollout to cohort C1 (50 nodes) at 08:55 UTC; rollout to C2 (200 nodes) started 09:00 UTC.
irene: Repro steps I used (quick):
```
# curl to canary region with tracing headers
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Canary: C2" \
  -H "X-Request-Trace: repro-790" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"long prompt ..."}' \
  https://api-inference.canary.redwood/v1/generate
```
charlie: I can spin up a stressproxy job that floods the hot path with the same seq distribution. Want me to run it against C2?
nina: Yes please — collect perf counters, fio, and /proc/interrupts during the run. Also capture nvprof on a sample instance if possible.
sam: Running stressproxy with --seq-dist=long --rps=50 now. Job id: sp-790-01.
ops-bot: stressproxy: job sp-790-01 scheduled on cohort C2 (1000 reqs, 5m).
support-oncall: Customer A reported errors earlier but now it's latency-only; no 5xxs. Their SLA p99 alert fired at 09:22.
irene: I pulled logs from a slow trace:
```
2026-03-17T09:21:43Z [runtime] trace=tr-790 id=req-42 stage=kv_fetch wait=3.2ms io_wait=120ms gpu_wait=4300ms
2026-03-17T09:21:43Z [runtime] thread=worker-9 syscall=epoll_wait wait=4300ms
```
charlie: Interesting — gpu_wait dominating. Could be starved by scheduling prefetch threads or by NVLINK congestion.
sam: In the stressproxy run I'm seeing p99 spike mirrors production: baseline 2.7s -> canary 6s. Stack traces show more time in rpc_send and nv_peer_copy.
nina: Hypothesis: the new affinity change increased cross-socket NVLINK traffic for long-seq batches. We should try disabling the affinity patch on a small cohort to validate.
irene: Agreed. Quick mitigations we can do now: 1) pin traffic for high-QPS tenants to older runtime variant 2) reduce default batch size for canary cohort 3) roll back stressproxy affinity change in a hotfix. Which is fastest?
charlie: Fastest is (1) and (2). We can set route override for 3 tenants via routing-config:
```
route.override: {
  "tenant_ids": ["acct-42","acct-9"],
  "runtime_version": "v2.14.2",
  "reason": "p99 regression C2"
}
```
sam: I pushed a temp routing override for acct-42 and acct-9. Monitoring...
ops-bot: routing: override applied for acct-42, acct-9 -> v2.14.2
support-oncall: Confirmed — latency for acct-42 p99 dropped back to ~2.9s within 90s. :white_check_mark:
irene: Good signal that runtime change is causal. Next: bisect the change in v2.14.3. Charlie, can you build a variant that toggles only the stressproxy affinity flag?
charlie: On it. Building v2.14.3-affinity-off now (artifact art-790-affoff). Will deploy as a tiny canary (10 nodes).
nina: Also collect kernel-level perf samples (perf record -F 99 -g) during the trial. Add nvprof tracing for one request.
charlie: Deployed aff-off to cohort C2-subset 10 nodes. stressproxy replayed. Early numbers: p99 -> 3.1s.
sam: That's a big win. Suggest we rollback the affinity change for full rollout and keep other runtime bits.
irene: Ops, what's the rollback window?
ops-bot: rollback-plan: automated rollback to v2.14.2 if p99 > 4.5s for >5m across C2. Manual rollback at will.
charlie: I'll open a hotfix PR that reverts only the affinity patch and we can cut v2.14.4.
nina: Meanwhile let's run an A/B with nvlink counters enabled to ensure downstream impact is limited. Add a cohort that has aff-on + reduced batch size to measure additive effects.
sam: Creating cohort C2b with aff-on + batch_size=4. stressproxy queued.
ops-bot: cohort C2b ready.
sam: Early read: aff-on + batch_size=4 still shows p99 ~4.2s, better than 6s but worse than 3.1s. So both affinity and batching matter.
irene: Decision: revert affinity change (v2.14.4) and then try gradual re-introduce with different NUMA policy. Charlie, pull request and assign to erin for approval.
charlie: PR opened: https://git.redwood.example/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/5573 — title: revert stressproxy affinity.
nina: Note for postmortem: add a test in our preflight that runs a short stressproxy long-seq job against canary to catch this interaction.
sam: I'll file the support ticket to inform impacted customers and note mitigations.
support-oncall: Sending a customer update now: "We've identified a runtime-affinity regression impacting p99 for long-generation workloads. We are reverting the affinity change and will update once rolled back. Apologies for the disruption."
irene: Thanks everyone. After rollback we'll keep monitoring 30m and then close. If anyone captures a divergent repro, paste trace id here.
charlie: Rollback initiated to v2.14.2 across C2 at 09:45 UTC.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback started for cohort C2.
nina: Monitoring dashboards... p99 trending down to baseline now.
sam: Good work. Follow-up items: 1) preflight stressproxy test 2) perf counters added to canary 3) better rollback auto-thresholds 4) postmortem with timeline and customer impact.
irene: I'll start the postmortem draft and allocate owner for each action item. Closing once 30m stable. :+1:
